events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a safety case filed by the rider. The complaint states that the driver repeatedly commented on the rider's body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe during the trip. The trace's SAFE-1 screen is settled (✓): a complaint describing inappropriate conduct and a rider feeling unsafe routes to a human, and the only allowed outcome is escalate [F3][SAFE-1].

The safety screen: I read the only text on the file — the complaint itself and the driver's post-trip statement "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened" [F4]. The complaint alleges unwanted sexual/personal comments and a request for the rider's number, i.e. harassment and a person feeling unsafe; nothing in the chat (there is none) or in the statement contains a threat, but the allegation of inappropriate conduct is squarely within SAFE-1. Safety concern is therefore suspected, and under SAFE-3 this tier may not rule, assign fault or recommend a resolution. I make no finding on whether the alleged conduct occurred: the rider's account appears only in the complaint and the driver's denial only in a statement written after the trip, with no in-app chat to corroborate either side [F3][F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-3].

What is disputed and what to check: whether the driver made body-related comments and asked for the rider's number during the approximately 17-minute trip (pickup 12:50, drop-off 13:07). The reviewer should weigh the rider's first-person account against the driver's general denial [F4], note that the in-app chat log is empty so there is neither corroboration nor an exculpatory record [F3], consider whether any call recording or other trip audio exists (the record shows none), and weigh credibility using both profiles — rider 129 d, 4.5, 0 disputes / 0 upheld [F5]; driver 327 d, 4.67, 999 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes / 0 upheld [F6]. No fraud flag is recorded on either party [F5][F6][TH-3].

The driving record is normal and decides nothing here: actual 17.1 km versus optimal 17.2 km (−0.1 km, −0%) and 17.0 min versus 23.6 min estimated [F1][F2]. The fare is a fixed $35.70 with no fare or excess-distance issue, so no monetary remedy arises; the amount is null and no route or billing clause bears on the safety allegation.

Evidence: the record contains no chat, no call recording and no other contemporaneous record of the alleged conduct, so the account cannot be verified either way [F1][F3][F4][TH-4]. The file goes up unruled, with no presumption in favour of either party, and no account action against the driver at this tier.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states that the driver repeatedly commented on her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe during the trip.

The complaint is a first-hand account of inappropriate conduct and of the rider feeling unsafe, which is a safety indicator rather than a fare or route question; the records show no in-app chat (F3), so nothing in the written record contradicts her account.

The driver's written statement denies only in general terms ('I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened') and is a claim, not a record; it does not rebut the rider's specific account of body comments and a request for her number.
Because the case contains a harassment and personal-safety allegation, this court may not rule, assign fault or recommend a resolution; the file must go to a human reviewer.

The rider has a clean record (129 days, 4.5 rating, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days), so her account carries credibility and no fraud flag raises the threshold, while the driver's history shows no prior upheld conduct complaint either.

weaknesses: The rider's account appears only in the complaint; there is no in-app chat record (F3) and no call recording, so the harassment allegation rests on her word alone against the driver's written denial (F4), and the system records cannot corroborate it.
The driver has a strong record (F6: 327 days, 4.67 rating, 999 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) which the reviewer will weigh against the rider's account under TH-3 credibility.

The trip itself shows nothing abnormal on the record (F1: actual 17.1 km vs optimal 17.2 km; F2: 17.0 min vs 23.6 min estimated), so no route, timing or fare fact supports or explains the safety concern.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a harassment and personal-safety allegation (unwanted comments about her body and a request for her number), which is exactly the kind of text SAFE-1 screens to a human: this case must be escalated, not decided by the system, and no fault may be assigned to my client by the automated process.

The record contains no in-app chat at all (F3 — 'No in-app chat messages between rider and driver'), so there is no contemporaneous written evidence of any comment, request for a number, or refusal; the only account in the record is the driver's own statement (F4) that he made small talk and nothing inappropriate happened.

The GPS record shows a completely ordinary, shortest-path trip: actual 17.1 km against a 17.2 km optimal route (−0.1 km, −0%) and 17.0 min against 23.6 min estimated (F1, F2) — no detour, no stop away from the route, and nothing in the driving record consistent with the rider feeling unsafe or wanting the trip to end early.

Because this is a safety-flagged case, the only permissible action for the automated tier is to prepare and hand over the case file; per SAFE-3 the AI may not rule, determine fault or recommend a resolution on a safety incident.

There is no fare, route or no-show issue to decide: the fare was a fixed $35.70 charge and the billing slice returns no fare facts, while the route and duration facts (F1, F2) show no excess distance at all — so no monetary remedy is computable or warranted from the record.

My client's record shows a 0.9-year-old account, 4.67 rating, 999 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes (F6), while the rider's profile shows 0 disputes in 90 days (F5); nothing in either profile supports a fraud finding or an account flag against the driver, and the profile facts could not decide this case in any event.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a direct, specific first-person account of unwanted comments and a request for her number; if the human reviewer credits it, my client's bare denial in F4 ('I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.') may look like a self-serving statement given there is no chat record (F3) to corroborate either version.

There is no in-app chat and therefore no recording or message log to disprove the rider's account; the absence of written evidence cuts both ways and the record cannot be verified from F3, which is why the case must go to a person under SAFE-1/TH-4 rather than be dismissed.
The rider's rating of 4.5 with 0 disputes in 90 days (F5) gives her account some credibility, so my client should not expect the escalation to end in a clean no-action finding.
Nothing in the record proves the absence of the alleged conduct — F1 and F2 only show the driving was normal, which is consistent with both parties' accounts and does not by itself refute the rider.

points.response: Agreed in substance: the complaint (a body-comment and number-request allegation) is exactly the safety indicator SAFE-1 screens, so the file goes to a person and no automated tier may assign fault to either side.

The absence of in-app chat (F3) is neutral, not exculpatory: RD-5-style rules and SAFE-1 deal with conduct, and the driver's post-trip statement (F4) is a denial written after the complaint, not a record that rebuts the rider's specific first-person account; an empty chat log cannot prove nothing was said aloud.

Conceded that the driving record is ordinary (F1: 17.1 km vs 17.2 km optimal; F2: 17.0 min vs 23.6 min), but harassment is not a route event, so no route clause (RD-1/RD-2) bears on the safety allegation either way; normal GPS (F1, F2) is consistent with both accounts and refutes neither.

Agreed: SAFE-3 bars the automated tier from ruling, fault-finding or recommending a resolution, so the only action I press for is escalation of the prepared case file with the F1/F2/F3/F4/F5/F6 record attached.

Conceded on money: the $35.70 is a fixed charge with no fare facts returned and no excess distance on the record (F1: −0.1 km vs optimal), so I ask no refund and no waiver — my sole request is escalate.

Agreed that profiles cannot decide the case (F5, F6): both parties show 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F5, F6), so I request no flag or account sanction against the driver — F5's clean rider history goes only to the credibility the human reviewer will weigh under TH-3.

I do not contest that the complaint says this (the complaint's words are on the file), but the complaint's text is a statement, not a system record: the only record of the trip's communication is F3, which shows no in-app chat at all, so the words of the complaint cannot be treated as established conduct.

The rider is right that a first-hand safety allegation routes this file to a human under SAFE-1 and that F3 contains nothing contradicting her — but that is the whole point: with no chat, no call recording and no corroborating record, neither account can be verified, so the file goes up unruled rather than decided against my client.

The rider's advocate concedes in their own weaknesses that the allegation rests on her word alone and that F4 is the driver's account; on this record the two accounts are word against word, and nothing in F3 or elsewhere proves the specific comments, so the reviewer — not this tier — must decide, per SAFE-3.
Conceded and identical to our own position: SAFE-3 bars this tier from ruling, assigning fault or recommending a resolution on a safety incident, so escalation is the only available action.

The profile facts are agreed and cut both ways: F5 (rider, 4.5, 0 disputes) and F6 (driver, 4.67, 999 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) show two credible parties with no fraud flag, which is exactly why no account flag under RD-6 can attach to my client and why credibility must be weighed by the human reviewer under TH-3, not scored here.
